messages.body_plain:
Hi Sumithra,
you can use regionCounts() function for that, check the function help and also an example is below:

data(methylKit)
example.file=system.file("extdata", "cpgi.hg18.bed.txt", package = "methylKit")

cpg.obj=read.feature.flank(example.file,feature.flank.name <http://feature.flank.name>=c("CpGi","shores")) # read CpGi  and shores

CpGi.methylRawList=regionCounts(methylObj=methylRawList.obj, regions=cpg.obj$CpGi)

The CpG island file should be in BED format and will be read in as GRanges object. If you can get GRanges object for CpG islands by other means you can also use that in regionCounts() function. If you want to learn how to download annotation files (the ones available in UCSC) in BED format see:
https://code.google.com/p/methylkit/#Downloading_Annotation_Files

Best,
Altuna

messages.subject: Memory usage
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I was wondering if there was an upper limit on the number of reads in total that can be analyzed efficiently with methylKit. For example, previous data sets that I have successfully analyzed have had about 60 million reads per sample group, but a new data set has about 120 million reads. The memory usage is becoming a problem when calling the unite function to find common sites between all samples. Previously memory usage has been only a few gigs of RAM, but with new data sets it maxes out memory (8 gigs) and uses about another 8-16 gigs of swap space and never finishes the function.  Is memory usage quadratic for this function? or is there something else going on? Any insights would be greatly appreciated.
Great program by the way. Have used quite a bit for a few different projects.
Thanks,
Jason

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jason,
How many samples you have in total? and are you using "min.per group" argument as well?

As a general advice, I suggest removing the unused objects from your environment with rm() and do garbage collection with gc(T).

Best,
Altuna

messages.subject: Re: annotation problem
messages.body_plain:
The problem seems to be that your CpG methylation and annotation file have a different chromosome naming convention, annotation file has "chr" string but not the CpG methylation files. You need to add the "chr" string to your CpG methylation files, so that they both have the same naming convention.

The new version(0.5.7) shouldn't require that the annotation files have the "chr" string in the chromosome names. Previous versions require the "chr" string in the annotation files even though you can read % methylation files without the "chr" string.

Best,
Altuna

You can get the percent methylation values from a methylRaw object as follows (in your example you named the variable as "CpGi.methylRawList" but it doesn't seem like a list, it is just one methylRaw object, so to avoid confusion I changed the name of the variable in the example below):

perc=100*(CpGi.methylRaw$numC/CpGi.methylRaw$coverage)
# perc includes % methylation values for each row in CpGi.methylRaw object

Then, you can use those values to subset your original methylRaw object. The following bit gets CpG islands that have above %30 methylation:

newobj=CpGi.methylRaw[perc>30,]

newobj

library(methylKit)

                system.file("extdata", "control2.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit") )

read.transcript.features() have one mandatory argument ( check ?read.transcript.features  and the documentation/examples)

It reads a bed file of gene/transcript annotations. That file is read into the memory so that you can later annotate your differentially methylated regions/bases as intergenic/intornic/promoter and exonic.

You are providing a CpG methylation file with the transcript file?

 gene.obj=read.transcript.features("/Users/essepf/Desktop/refseq.hg18.bed.txt")
